query: The Damp Stove {A rowing crew comes in off the lake soaked to the skin, laughing through chattering teeth. The boathouse stove is cold, and the kindling basket is wet through.|The crew again, wetter than last time: someone caught a crab and took the boat over. The kindling has been left out in the rain, as usual.|Another soaking. The crew have started looking at you when they come in, and then at the stove.} Run to the boatman's loft for dry wood {You run up to the loft and back with an armful of dry wood. By the time the stove's going you're as wet as they are, from the sweat.|The loft ladder, in the dark, with an armful of wood. You make it. The crew make room for you on the bench.|The loft ladder is the worst part. The crew cheer you down it like a returning hero.} Lend your scarf and leave them to it {You give your scarf to the one with blue lips and walk back up to the castle with a cold neck. You'll get the scarf back. Probably.|You hand round your scarf and your sympathy and leave them to it. The scarf comes back a week later, smelling of lake.|Scarf, a joke, and goodnight. They wave you off, still shivering, still laughing.} Dry the kindling with a flame {You hold a flame under the wet kindling until it steams, then catches. The crew crowd the stove and somebody's lake-cold hand finds your shoulder in thanks.|A flame, coaxed small and patient, and the kindling catches in a fizz of steam. The crew name the stove after you. It's not a compliment, exactly.|You dry the whole basket in one long breath of fire. The crew offer you a seat in the boat next week. You decline, warmly.}
